COD.hook: The Congo is the deepest river in the world, over 220m in places — and the country holds most of the world's cobalt.
COD.place: The vast heart of Africa astride the equator, with only a 40km squeeze of Atlantic coast.

COG.hook: Its capital Brazzaville faces Kinshasa across the river — the closest pair of capital cities anywhere in the world.
COG.place: On the Atlantic west of DR Congo. This is the smaller Congo; the two stare at each other across the water.

AGO.hook: Portuguese-speaking, and split in two — the oil-rich Cabinda exclave is cut off from the rest by a strip of DR Congo.
AGO.place: On the Atlantic below DR Congo, with the separate Cabinda enclave sitting to its north.

CMR.hook: Called Africa in miniature — desert, rainforest, savanna, mountains and coast in one country, with both English and French official.
CMR.place: At the crook of the Gulf of Guinea, where West Africa turns the corner and heads south.

TCD.hook: Lake Chad has lost about 90% of its surface area since the 1960s — the country is named after a lake that is nearly gone.
TCD.place: Landlocked in north-central Africa, running from deep Sahara down into the Sahel.

SSD.hook: The newest country in the world, independent in 2011 — and the Sudd wetland at its centre is among the largest on Earth.
SSD.place: Landlocked below Sudan, between Ethiopia and the Central African Republic.

CAF.hook: Sits almost exactly at the geographic centre of the continent, and is among the least visited countries on the planet.
CAF.place: Landlocked in the middle of Africa, below Chad and above DR Congo.

GAB.hook: About 88% forest, and in 2002 it turned a tenth of the entire country into national parks in a single stroke.
GAB.place: On the equator on the Atlantic coast, below Cameroon and west of the Republic of the Congo.

GNQ.hook: The only African country with Spanish as an official language — and its capital is not on the mainland but on an island.
GNQ.place: A mainland slice plus islands in the Gulf of Guinea; Malabo sits on Bioko, closer to Cameroon than to its own territory.

STP.hook: Two volcanic islands on the equator that were once the largest cocoa producer in the world — from almost nothing to first place and back.
STP.place: In the Gulf of Guinea off Gabon, straddling the equator.
